_about: The closed list of named map fixtures (docs/turn-budget-and-fixtures-plan.md, Part 2). Read and validated by rules/fixtures.py; a bad entry raises at load with the fix named. Each kind declares ONLY properties the engine reads today (occupies, low, cover, stair, reached_by, climb_dc, opening, see_through) plus phase-2 data it records but does not yet act on (flammable, breakable, movable, burns, swim, hardness, hp). Page numbers are the Core Rulebook (CRB). 'house rule' marks a number the book does not print.

_fields.occupies: which existing geometry this kind may type: blocked, difficult, raised, open (a square left walkable), overhead. Phase 1 never changes a square's geometry to make a fixture fit.
_fields.low: a low obstacle: blocks movement like any solid square, but sight passes over it and it gives cover, never total cover (CRB p.195: 'a low obstacle (such as a wall no higher than half your height) provides cover'). The grid reads it as a parapet one level above the floor.
_fields.cover: what standing behind it gives: cover (+4 AC, +2 Reflex, CRB p.195), soft (creatures only in the book, p.196), or none.
_fields.stair: walkable between levels: a creature with no climb or fly speed may walk from the floor to the raised fixture it reaches (reached_by).
_fields.reached_by: raised ground that a body walks onto by this kind (a gallery is reached by a stair), rather than climbs.
_fields.climb_dc: the Climb check to get up onto it (CRB p.90 table), or null. Phase 1 names it in the refusal; the check itself is phase 2.
_fields.placed: false: in the vocabulary (the reader may name it, a world may author it), but phase 1 has no geometry to lay it on.
_fields.narratable: true: the reader naming it in a room with none lets code place one on a free square.

stair.name: a stair
stair.source: CRB p.415 (Stairs: steep stairs are difficult terrain; not applied, phase 2). Walking up a stair needs no Climb check: the book has no check for it.

gallery.name: a gallery
gallery.source: Raised walkway (floorplan 'ledge'). Climbing its face without the stair: CRB p.90, 'a typical wall in a dungeon', DC 20 (house rule choice of row).

door.name: a door
door.source: CRB p.173 Table 7-14, simple wooden door: hardness 5, 10 hp, break DC 13. Open/shut as state is phase 2.

window.name: a window
window.source: CRB p.173 Table 7-13, glass: hardness 1, 1 hp per inch. A window needs a wall square to sit in; phase 2.

table.name: a table
table.source: Cover from a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Hardness and hp: wood, 1 inch thick, CRB p.173 Table 7-13 (house rule thickness).

counter.name: a counter
counter.source: A bar or shop counter: a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Wood 2 inches thick, CRB p.173 Table 7-13 (house rule thickness).

stall.name: a stall
stall.source: A market stall: a trestle counter under an awning, a low obstacle like a counter, CRB p.195. Wood 1 inch thick, CRB p.173 Table 7-13 (house rule thickness).

barrel.name: a barrel
barrel.source: About waist high on a Medium creature: a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Wooden staves, CRB p.173 Table 7-13. Flammable only when it holds oil or spirits (phase 2).

crate.name: a crate
crate.source: Low obstacle, CRB p.195. Climb onto it: CRB p.90, 'a surface with ledges to hold on to and stand on', DC 10 (house rule choice of row). Wood, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

rack.name: a rack
rack.source: A weapon rack, wine rack or shelving: taller than a Medium creature, so solid (blocks sight; total cover when it hides you completely, CRB p.196). Climb: CRB p.90 'adequate handholds and footholds', DC 15.

bookshelf.name: a bookshelf
bookshelf.source: Its own kind rather than a rack: a library's stacks, solid to the ceiling. CRB p.173: fire may do full damage to paper. Climb: CRB p.90, DC 15. The CRB's only bookcase is a secret door's disguise (p.412).

hearth.name: a hearth
hearth.source: A stone hearth: low obstacle, CRB p.195. Stone, CRB p.173 Table 7-14 masonry wall (house rule). Entering the fire (CRB p.444 catching on fire) is phase 2.

chandelier.name: a chandelier
chandelier.source: Overhead; swinging from it is phase 2. No CRB rule (house rule territory).

cart.name: a cart
cart.source: Its side is a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Climb onto the bed: CRB p.90 DC 10 (house rule choice of row). Wood, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

crane.name: a crane
crane.source: A dockside crane or headframe. Lifting with it is phase 2.

water.name: standing water
water.source: Shallow water is difficult terrain (CRB p.427 marsh: shallow bog costs 2 squares). Deeper water is rules/water.py's, not a fixture's.

rubble.name: rubble
rubble.source: Dense rubble costs 2 squares to enter, CRB p.411.

mast.name: a mast
mast.source: A ship's mast on the centre line (Ultimate Combat pp.184-185 gives each vessel's masts): solid, the thing to put between you and them, cover CRB p.195. Climbed by its rigging, not up the bare pole: see rigging. Wood, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

rigging.name: the rigging
rigging.source: The shrouds and their ratlines at the rail abaft each mast, laid as a square 10 ft up. CRB p.90 Climb table, DC 10: 'a surface with ledges to hold on to and stand on, such as a very rough wall or a ship's rigging'.

rope.name: a coil of rope
rope.source: Line coiled down on a deck or a quay: underfoot clutter, difficult terrain like light undergrowth, CRB p.425 (house rule choice of row).

hatch.name: a hatch
hatch.source: A deck hatch and the ladder under it, walked onto like floor; going down it is the ship's next room (rules/ships.py places_of). Hardness and hp as a simple wooden door, CRB p.173 Table 7-14 (house rule).

helm.name: the helm
helm.source: The wheel or tiller aft, where Ultimate Combat p.184 puts a ship's driving device ('the nine squares around the steering wheel, typically located at the aft of the ship'). Waist high: a low obstacle, CRB p.195.

capstan.name: a capstan
capstan.source: The drum the anchor cable is hove in on, forward on the deck. Waist high: a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Wood, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

anchor.name: an anchor
anchor.source: Catted at the bow. A low obstacle, CRB p.195. Iron, hardness 10, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

bench.name: a rowing bench
bench.source: A rower's bench at the side, where a longship's forty and a galley's 140 rowers sit (Ultimate Combat pp.184-185). A low obstacle, CRB p.195; wood, CRB p.173.

boat.name: a ship's boat
boat.source: A rowboat lashed amidships or tied up at a quay (Ultimate Combat's rowboat is a Large vehicle). Its gunwale is a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Rowing it is phase 2.

rail.name: the rail
rail.source: The gunwale: laid on the squares of sea beside the hull, so a line between two people on deck never crosses it and a line from outboard does, at or under its top (a low obstacle, CRB p.195). Those squares are water (swim): a swimmer holds them beside the hull, and going over the side is a move into them, rules/water.py's table.

sea.name: the sea
sea.source: Open water past the rail or a quay's edge: not walked on (going in is rules/water.py's place, not this board's). Its top is the water's surface, a level under the planking, so sight and shots pass over it and it covers nobody.

bollard.name: a bollard
bollard.source: A mooring post on a quay's lip. Knee to waist high: a low obstacle, CRB p.195. Wood, CRB p.173 Table 7-13.

_places_about: Which kinds type which existing geometry, by the spot slug floorplan.BY_SPOT is keyed on, then by terrain. solid types blocked clumps (the biggest clump takes the first kind, and so on, cycling); rough types difficult squares; raised types the isolated raised squares of a 'scatter' place. A 'ledge' place's raised band is always a gallery reached by a stair. A place with no row types nothing but its gallery: pillars, trees and gravestones are not fixtures.
